vast-ai-epyc-7c13-t0129.description: Vast.ai instance 37924958 (AMD EPYC 7C13 64-Core, 32 effective vCPUs, 64 GB RAM, 1x Tesla V100 idle, Virginia US, $0.1911/hr total = $0.1733/hr base + $0.0178/hr storage for the 64 GB disk). Final cost = full instance lifetime from ready_at 2026-05-26T14:46:55Z to destroyed_at 2026-05-26T19:49:52Z (duration_hours=5.0492, dph=$0.1911 -> cost=$0.9650). Per the caller's teardown instruction, total_duration_hours is computed from ready_at (not created_at); the additional 22 s from created_at to ready_at adds ~$0.001 which is rounded into total_cost_usd. The NSGA-II cost_watchdog's in-driver final_cost_usd=$0.6469 covered only the active 3.385 h NSGA-II run window (12,184 s wallclock per the run log final HV line). The additional $0.318 covers the lifetime before NSGA-II launch (apt install + pip dependencies for NEURON 8.2.7 / pymoo 0.6.1.6 / dill / numpy / pandas / scipy / matplotlib / pydantic / tqdm / sklearn + t0080 MOD compile + t0024 DSGC MOD compile + t0129 code SCP + Carter-Bean smoke-gate, ~38 min) and the post-run window between gen-60 exit and teardown (wrap-up SCP downloads + orchestrator hand-off, ~1.07 h). 60-gen ceiling reached cleanly with NSGA2_EXIT=0, pop=96, n_eval_seeds=3, n_directions=2 antipodal 0/180 deg, single seed 3517. Instance destroyed via 'vastai destroy instance 37924958 --yes' in step 010_teardown.

note: Final post-teardown cost. Two figures are recorded across the task: (1) the NSGA-II driver's in-flight cost_watchdog reported final_cost_usd=$0.6469 at gen 60 exit -- this only covers the 3.385 h active NSGA-II window (12,184 s per the run log final HV line); (2) the full instance lifetime from ready to destroy is 5.0492 h at $0.1911/hr = $0.9650 (machine_log.json ready_at -> destroyed_at per the caller's teardown instruction). The $0.318 delta covers ~38 min of pre-NSGA-II setup (apt + pip + MOD compile + smoke-gate) and ~1.07 h of post-run wrap-up (SCP downloads + teardown idle). costs.json totals reflect option (2) -- the actual Vast.ai spend -- per remote_machines_specification.md. The Virginia US 7C13 instance is 4% more expensive per hour than t0126's sister partition ($0.1911 vs $0.1844) because t0129 took the 64 GB disk partition vs t0126's 40 GB. watchdog_tripped=false; the full 60-generation ceiling was reached with NSGA2_EXIT=0.
